item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00433","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C05","C08","C23"],"selected_candidate_label":"C05","confidence":0.96,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C05 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template for the child. Both letters answer proposals for direct high-level negotiations with the Soviet leadership, accept such negotiations in principle, insist that they be prepared through diplomatic and foreign-minister channels, and warn that an inadequately prepared summit may fail and worsen tensions. They also proceed through closely parallel substantive subjects: Germany and Berlin, nuclear testing, broader disarmament, international inspection and control, and United Nations machinery. C08 closely parallels the summit-preparation passages but supplies less of the child's broader sequence; C23 contains related language about preliminary diplomatic contacts but is more remote.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"unless such negotiations are carefully prepared beforehand they risk failure and may lead to deterioration of the situation... negotiations of the kind proposed... [must] have careful preparation but also a reasonable chance of success","parent_excerpt":"Preparatory work, with good will on both sides, is a prerequisite to success. High level meetings... involve a danger of disillusionment, dejection and increased distrust if in fact the meetings are ill-prepared","explanation":"Distinctive shared warning that an inadequately prepared summit could fail and affirmatively worsen international relations."},{"child_excerpt":"The Foreign Ministers of the Western powers are meeting in Washington tomorrow... This will provide an opportunity for serious talks... The channels of diplomacy are open for the exploration of constructive steps","parent_excerpt":"It would be essential that prior to such a meeting these complex matters should be worked on in advance through diplomatic channels and by our Foreign Ministers","explanation":"Both prescribe the same preparatory machinery: diplomatic channels and foreign-minister discussions before negotiations at the highest level."},{"child_excerpt":"We wish to reaffirm... our belief that test ban negotiations should be resumed separately from negotiations on general and complete disarmament... The United States is pleased to note... the importance of an effective system of inspection and control","parent_excerpt":"Let us also end the now unrestrained production of nuclear weapons... we stop the testing of nuclear weapons... The capacity to verify the fulfillment of commitments is of the essence in all these matters","explanation":"Both move from summit diplomacy into nuclear testing and general disarmament, treating effective verification and control as indispensable."},{"child_excerpt":"We endorse the Declaration's reference to the rights of all nations to unity, self-determination, and independence... We presume that these principles apply equally to the people of Germany and Berlin.","parent_excerpt":"I therefore urge that we now proceed vigorously to bring about the reunification of Germany by free elections... The second situation... is that of the countries of Eastern Europe... [whose] peoples... should have the right to choose the form of government under which they would live","explanation":"The child adapts C05's use of universal self-determination principles as an argument concerning Germany and Berlin."}]}
